why: Review of the 37 open-reader problems map-3 could not map (and 122 in map-4): every one was the harness's field markers or its reasoning field judged against the instruction text's own output-format paragraph, which the harness overrides. Not candidate failures; the format codes now say so. The codes themselves are otherwise unchanged.

amendments.name: MALFORMED_STRUCTURED_LIST_OR_SORTING_DEFECT
amendments.before: Do not use when the entire evidence section header or mandatory field is missing (use MISSING_REQUIRED_OUTPUT_FIELD_OR_MARKER).
amendments.after: Do not use when the entire evidence section header or mandatory field is missing (use the omitted-section codes). The `[[ ## field ## ]]` markers around output fields and a `reasoning` field are the execution harness's own output format, declared in the instructions section and needed to parse the output; using them instead of a plainer layout described in the instruction text is not a failure of any kind.
amendments.reason: all 37 problems map-3 could not map, and 94 of map-4's 122, were the harness's field markers or its `reasoning` field judged against the instruction text's own 'Output Format' paragraph; the mapper reached for this code

amendments.name: OMITTED_EVIDENCE_CATEGORIZATION_SECTION
amendments.before: Do not use when missing a system boundary marker at the very end of response, or when failing to explain multi-hop reasoning logic.
amendments.after: Do not use when missing a system boundary marker at the very end of response, or when failing to explain multi-hop reasoning logic. The `[[ ## field ## ]]` markers around output fields and a `reasoning` field are the execution harness's own output format, declared in the instructions section and needed to parse the output; using them instead of a plainer layout described in the instruction text is not a failure of any kind.
amendments.reason: 16 of map-4's unmapped problems reached for this code; same harness artefact

amendments.name: MISSING_TERMINAL_COMPLETION_MARKER
